title: 'It's just who I am' - Man says he confronted Alta Vista murder suspect as he harassed teenager weeks prior to killings
subtitle: "It's such a nightmare. I'm still kind of in shock. It makes me wonder if he had weapons on him when I confronted him."
article: In early May, a man was working with a landscaping crew in Overbrook when he noticed another young man walking close to a teenage girl.
He watched them walk past the job site on Whitton Street. Minutes later, the girl walked purposefully back towards the site, crying, with the young man in pursuit.
The young man was clearly harassing the girl, who was covering her ears and screaming, according to the landscaper, whose identify is protected by a publication ban.
The Ottawa Citizen's best journalism, delivered directly to your inbox by 7 p.m. on weekdays.

The young man was Joshua Graves. The 21-year-old would be shot dead by police on the evening of June 27 in the act of stabbing 19-year-old Catherine Ready. He had already killed her mother, Anne-Marie, 50, and her sister, Jasmine, who was 15.

That double homicide happened just three days after Graves was released by an Ottawa justice of the peace following his arrest on charges of criminal harassment, assault and sexual assault. The landscaper was to be a witness in that case based on his experience on Whitton Street.
It was about 4 p.m. when the man decided to involve himself in whatever was happening between Graves and the young girl.

"It was when she was obviously distressed that it clicked in that they were not friends," he said of his decision to get involved. "That's when it didn't sit right. That's when it's like, 'Ok, if nobody else is going to do anything, I'll do something."
The man is 6'3 tall, and Graves fled as he stood up and approached them.
"He just ran away," he said.
He described Graves as skinny, with shaggy dark brown hair and an ear piercing. "He looked like a typical teenager."
The man asked the girl, now curled into a ball on the sidewalk, if he could sit down and talk.
"I was just trying to calm her down," he explained. "My mother is a social worker and she's always asking me, 'When are you going to be a social worker?'"
The girl, 16, said she had met Graves two years ago while she was a Grade 9 student. He was interested in her, but she didn't want anything to do with him after she found out that he was 19.

He sexually harassed her online, the man said, and after she blocked his posts, he showed up outside one of her classes and followed her home. According to the man, Graves told the girl she couldn't just block him and cut him out of her life. "I'll always be here, I'll always find you," he said, according to the account given by the man.
The girl told him that Graves was sharing his graphic sexual fantasies about her when she fled from him on Whitton Street.
The man walked the girl home, and encouraged her to report the incident to police.
"I said, 'If you want something done, you're going to have to call law enforcement.' She was worried about retaliation."

After he returned to his job site, and was packing up to go home, the man was approached by the girl and her mother. The girl's mother asked him to recount what happened. She vowed to go to the authorities and took the man's name and number for police to contact as a potential witness.
He was contacted by police later that same evening, and gave a formal statement two weeks later.
Late last month, the man recognized Graves' name when he read a story online about the double homicide in Alta Vista. He was relieved the 16-year-old was not among the victims.

"I just said, 'What the hell?,'" he remembers. "That's just not something I really expected. It's such a nightmare. I'm still kind of in shock. It makes me wonder if he had weapons on him when I confronted him."
The man said he was reprimanded by his landscaping company for getting involved in the incident.

"I didn't care. I said, 'You know what, this is why sh** like this happens all the time. It's because nobody does anything...If somebody's upset and in distress, I'm going to try to comfort them. It's just who I am."
